[Page 58]

**Sūrat Yūnus**

It is Meccan according to the well-known view, though some scholars excepted three verses from it: 1 ﴿So perhaps you will abandon﴾, ﴿Is one who has clear proof from his Lord﴾, and ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾. It is said that these were revealed in Medina. Ibn al-Furs and al-Sakhawi related that from its beginning up to the end of the fortieth verse is Meccan and the rest is Medinan. There are two reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both. Ibn Mardawayh transmitted through al-ʿAwfī from him, and through Ibn Jurayj from ʿAṭāʾ from him, that it is Meccan. He also transmitted through ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ from his father from him that it is Medinan. The view relied upon by the majority is the first report. Its number of verses is one hundred and nine according to all, except the Shami reading, according to which it has one hundred and ten verses.

Its connection to Sūrat Barāʾa (al-Tawba) is that the first (Sūrat Barāʾa) ends with the mention of the Messenger (ﷺ), and this one (Sūrat Yūnus) begins with him. Also, in the first there is an explanation of what the hypocrites say when a surah of the Qur'an is revealed, and in this one there is an explanation of what the disbelievers say about the Qur'an, where He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it"﴾, and the verse. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it."﴾ Also, in the first there is a censure of the hypocrites for not repenting and not taking heed when affliction strikes them, in His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice? Then they do not repent, nor do they remember﴾, according to one of the opinions. In this one there is a censure of the one who is struck by affliction, then turns back, and that is in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us for a harm that touched him﴾. And in His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon it a violent wind, and the waves come to them from everywhere, and they think they are encompassed, they call upon Allah, devoting religion sincerely to Him﴾, up to His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿But when He has delivered them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right﴾.

Also, in the first (Sūrat Barāʾa) there is the disavowal of the Messenger (ﷺ) from the polytheists together with the command to fight them in the most complete manner. In this one there is his disavowal (ﷺ) from their deeds, but without a command to fight. Rather, he was commanded therein, upon him be prayer and peace, to declare the disavowal in a manner that conveys turning away and leaving them to their way, as it has been said, in contrast to what is in the first. This is also a kind of connection, and it is in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And if they deny you, say, "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do."﴾ and other than that.

It is strange that al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī, may Allah have mercy on him, did not perceive in Tanāsuq al-Durar the connection between the two surahs, nor mention the connection between this surah and Sūrat al-Aʿrāf. Yet in the fallings (al-Asqāṭ) there may be what is not found in the pearl-strings (al-Asfāṭ).

(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Alif-Lām-Rā﴾: the ra is read with emphasis (tafkhīm) as an open vowel, and this is the original reading. Abū ʿAmr and some readers inclined it (imāla), treating the alif of the ra as the alif that has been converted from a ya, so they incline it to indicate its origin. The purpose of inclination here is to avert the suspicion that ra is a letter, as the grammarians have stated that letters cannot take inclination. Warsh read it between-between (bayn bayn). What is meant by (al-Rā), according to what a group related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, is "I am Allah, the Seer." In another report, it is a part of al-Raḥmān, and its completion is ḥm wn. From Qatāda it is related that it is a part of al-Rāḥim, which is one of the names of the Qur'an. It has also been said that these are names of the letters known from the letters of the alphabet, brought in succession in the pattern of enumeration, in the manner of challenge. According to this, they have no place in terms of i'rāb (grammatical case analysis), and the discussion of them and their like is well known.)

[Page 59]

Most scholars hold that it is the name of the surah. Thus its place is nominative, as it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: this surah is named such-and-such. This is more apparent than the nominative reading as a subject (mubtada'), because knowledge of the naming has not preceded it, so its due is to inform of it, not to make it the title of the topic, since that depends on the addressee's knowledge of the attribution. The pointing to it before its mention has occurred is because it is treated as present, given that it is on the wing of mention, as is said in deeds: "This is what so-and-so has bought." The accusative reading has also been permitted, with an implied verb suitable to the context, such as "recite" or "read." The word ﴿That﴾ is a demonstrative referring to it. Either on the assumption that (al-Rā) is recited as an enumeration, in which case the presence of its material has taken the place of its mention, so it is pointed to as if it were said: "These words composed from the kind of these letters spread out, etc." Or on the assumption that it is the name of the surah, in which case the demonstrative has been used after the mention of its name, or the command to mention it, or to recite it. The sense of distance in the demonstrative is to indicate the elevated status of its grandeur. Its place is nominative as a subject whose predicate is the saying of the Exalted, the Majestic: ﴿the verses of the Book﴾. On the assumption that (al-Rā) is a subject, it is either a second subject or an apposition to the first. The meaning is: they are particular verses from it, translated by an independent noun. The purpose of stating its partiality from it is to describe it with the excellent attributes and perfect qualities pointed to in its possession. The Book (al-Kitāb) may mean either the entire great Qur'an, even if it had not yet been sent down, either in terms of its determination and realization in knowledge or on the Tablet, or in terms of its being sent down all at once to the House of Honor (Bayt al-ʿIzza) from the lowest heaven. Or it may mean the entire Qur'an being revealed at that time and understood among people, for just as it is applied to the individual collective, it is also applied to the collection of what was revealed in each such period. Shaykh al-Islām said so.

You know that the well-known view from the early scholars is to commit the meaning of (al-Rā) and its like to Allah, exalted is He. Since its meaning has not become clear, there is no sense in addressing its i'rāb. They have mentioned that the demonstrative may refer to the verses of this surah, or to the verses of the Qur'an. The Book may mean the surah, or it may mean the Qur'an. Thus the cases are four. The first: the reference to the verses of the Qur'an with the Book meaning the surah. This is not valid except by specifying some verses or by a distant interpretation. The second is the reverse, and there is no objection to it. The third: the reference to the verses of the surah, with the Book meaning the surah. The fourth: the reference to the verses of the Qur'an, with the Book meaning the Qur'an. The statement's benefit in relation to both is in terms of the attribute of the Book that follows. It has been permitted to point to the verses, even if they are not mentioned, because they are treated as present, as in the example mentioned just above. In the Amālī of Ibn al-Ḥājib it is stated that the pointed-to thing does not need to be present and existing in the flesh; it suffices that it exists in the mind. In the Kashshāf, in its commentary on His saying: ﴿This is the parting between me and you﴾, there is something that supports this. The word ﴿that﴾ is preferred for what the Shaykh indicated, and because it is in the status of the absent in one respect. What they have mentioned is not free from unease. As for taking the Book to refer to the books that came before the Qur'an, such as the Torah and the Gospel and others, as Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatāda, it is extremely remote, so reflect.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the Wise﴾ is an attribute of the Book. It is described thus because it includes wisdom. So by "the Wise" is meant one possessing wisdom, with the form being for attribution, like "lābin" and "tāmir" (having milk, having dates). It may also be considered that the Book is likened to a speaking person who speaks wisdom, by way of metaphor by allusion (istiʿāra bil-kināya), and the affirmation of wisdom is an indicator of it. It has also been permitted that its description with this is because it is a wise speech, so the meaning is that its speaker is wise, and the figurative usage is in the attribution, like "his night stands and his day fasts." It has also been said that it is because its verses are decisive (muḥkama), none of which has been abrogated by another book, so fa'īl is in the sense of mufʿal. What it has in its favor and against it has already been discussed.

[p. 60]

﴿Is it a wonder for mankind?﴾ The hamzah (interrogative particle) here expresses disapproval of their amazement, and also serves to make the listeners marvel at it, because it has been placed where it does not belong. By "mankind" is meant the disbelievers of the Arabs. The expression by the general term "mankind" does not touch on their disbelief, which is the basis of their amazement, as it does later, in order to establish the partnership between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and them in what it involves, and to specify the basis of the amazement in their claim, then to clarify their error and show the falsehood of their claim by introducing the disapproval. The lam is connected to a deleted element that functions as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of ﴿wonder﴾, as is the rule when a qualifier of an indefinite noun is placed before it. It has been said that it is connected to "wonder" on the basis of the well-known broadening in adverbial phrases (ẓarf). Some of them made it connected to it not in the manner of an object (mafʿūl), but in the manner of specification (tabyīn), as in the words of the poet:

"I marvel at the course of time between me and her,"

and as in ﴿Come, I am ready for you﴾ and "Watering to you." Like this, it is permissible to place it before the verbal noun (maṣdar). You know that this is a statement of attachment to an implied element in reality. It has been said that it is connected to it because it has the meaning of "that which amazes," and when a verbal noun has the meaning of a passive or active participle, it is permissible to place its complement before it. It was also permitted that it be connected to kāna, even though it is a defective verb (kāna al-nāqiṣah), on the basis of its permissibility. "Wonder" is the predicate of kāna, placed before its subject, which is the statement of Him, glorified is He: ﴿that We revealed﴾, because it is the target of the disapproval and amazement, and in order to create suspense for what comes later, and because the subject contains a kind of detail, so placing it first preserves the original order, and yet there is some disruption in the harmony of the parts of the noble composition.

Ibn Mas'ud read "wonder" (ʿajabun) with a nominative ending, as the subject of kāna, and it is indefinite, while the predicate is ﴿that We revealed﴾, which is definite, because "that" (anna) together with the verb is in the sense of a verbal noun annexed to a definite noun. So it is like the words of Ḥassān:

"As if a wine from amid a cup, whose blend is honey and water."

Some of them interpreted it as an inversion (qalb). There is disagreement over whether this is accepted unconditionally or only when it includes a subtle meaning. The reliable position is the requirement that it include such a meaning, and that is not evident here. It is reported from Ibn Jinni that he said: "That was permissible in the verse only because honey and water are two kinds, so it is as if he said: 'Its blend is honey and water.' The indefinite of a kind conveys the same meaning as its definite." Do you not see that you say: "I went out, and behold, a lion is at the door," meaning "and behold, the lion is at the door"? There is no difference between them, because in both places you do not mean a specific lion. For this reason it is not permissible in your saying: "Standing one is your brother," or "Sitting one is your father," because there is no meaning of the kind in "sitting" and "standing" that would bring together the sense of their indefinite and definite forms.

The meaning of the verse according to this is: "Was it a wonder to mankind, this kind of action, which is amazement?" It is not hidden that the verbal noun resulting here is the verbal noun annexed to a definite noun, as you have heard, so considering it as prefixed with the definite article of kind is contrary to the apparent meaning. Some have permitted the predicate of the definite noun to be an indefinite noun, specifically in the chapter on the abrogating particles (nawāsikh), whether or not there is a negation or something in its ruling. Ibn Jinni permits this if there is a negation or something in its ruling, and does not permit it otherwise. In the verse, the interrogative of disapproval has already preceded the abrogating particle, and it is in the ruling of negation. More than one scholar has preferred that kāna be a complete verb (kāna al-tāmmah), with "wonder" as its subject, and ﴿that We revealed﴾ with an implied preposition connected to "wonder," meaning "for that We revealed," or "from that We revealed," or it is a substitute for it, a substitution of the whole for the whole, or a substitution of inclusion. The disapproval is directed at it being a wonder, not at its occurrence. The substitution being in the ruling of removing the substituted element does not mean that it is entirely discarded, as is established in its proper place.

In al-Lawāmiḥ, it is restricted to saying that ﴿for mankind﴾ is the predicate of kāna. This was criticized as weak in meaning, because it conveys the denial that it proceeded from mankind, not absolutely. There is clear weakness in it, so understand. It was said "for mankind" and not "among mankind," in order to indicate that they took it as an object of wonder for themselves, and there is in this an increase in the condemnation of their state that is not hidden.

﴿to a man from among them﴾, meaning, to a human from their own kind, like His statement, exalted is He, quoting them: ﴿Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ and His statement, glorified is He: ﴿Had our Lord willed, He would have sent down angels.﴾ Or, it means "to a man from among the most distinguished of their lineages," in terms of wealth, not in terms of ancestry, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among their notables, and he had a position among them that could not be rejected. So it is like their saying:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?﴾

It is reported in some narrations that they used to say: "The wonder is that Allah, exalted is He, did not find a messenger to send to the people except the orphan of Abu Talib." The wonder is due to their extreme ignorance. As for their first statement, they did not know that the sending of an angel occurs only when those sent to are angels, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ As for the general mass of humans, they are far from being worthy of conversing with angels, because such conversation is bound to affinity, so sending an angel to them conflicts with the wisdom upon which the orbit of creation and legislation revolves. What wisdom requires is the sending of an angel from among them to the elite who are specially devoted to pure souls, strengthened by holy power, and connected to both the spiritual and the corporeal worlds, so that they may be able to receive and to transmit. This follows from the eternal preparedness, as is not hidden.

As for their second statement, the criterion for selection for revelation to a person is precedence in being characterized by what you have come to know, and being first in attaining virtues and acquiring noble qualities, both innate and acquired. There is no doubt for anyone that the Prophet (ﷺ) has the highest share of this, rather he, peace and blessings be upon him, has in it the utmost of the farthest ends and the ultimate of the most distant limits. The one who saw him says:

"Never has my eye seen anyone more beautiful than you, and no woman has ever given birth to one like you.
You were created free from every defect, as if you were created as you wished."

Likewise he says: "Even if your self were to be portrayed, it would not add to what is in you of nobility of character." As for precedence in worldly leadership and being first in attaining lowly worldly fortunes, it has no bearing on that at all. Rather, it often hinders it. How excellent is the saying of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, from among verses:

"But whoever is granted wisdom is deprived of wealth;
they are two opposites, far apart in their separation."

As for what they mentioned of orphanhood, if it is traced back to what is in the verse according to the second interpretation, then its falsehood is its falsehood. If they meant that the very state of orphanhood prevents revelation to him, peace and blessings be upon him, then that is even more evidently false and clearly absurd. How subtle is what has been said: "The most precious of pearls is the one that is orphaned." It was also said to al-Hasan: "Why did Allah, exalted is He, make the Prophet (ﷺ) an orphan?" He said: "So that no creature would have a favor over him, for Allah, glorified is He, is the One who sheltered him, educated him, and raised him, (ﷺ)."

﴿from among them﴾. The second of the two possibilities mentioned earlier regarding His statement, glorified is He: ﴿to a man from among them﴾, according to the interpretation we have mentioned, is what the author of al-Kashshaf intended, but al-Jalal al-Suyuti did not accept it and claimed that avoiding it is preferable. Then he said: "What I hold concerning the explanation of this is that what is meant is 'to one well known among them, whose lineage, nobility, trustworthiness, and chastity they know,' as He, glorified is He, said at the end of the previous surah: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves.﴾ For this is the very place of the disapproval of the wonder. This would be the reason why this surah was placed after that one, and why the beginning of this one is linked to the end of that one. A similar example is ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among them, but they denied him﴾ and ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among them﴾, and so on, to the end of what he said." It was criticized as not evident, because although it is greater than what was mentioned, the context requires showing their disbelief, their humiliation, and the belittling of the one whom Allah, exalted is He, honored and magnified. What the occasion of revelation requires is that the first interpretation is specified here. Ibn Jarir and others reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that he said: "When Allah, exalted is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, the Arabs denied that, or those among them who denied it said: 'Allah, exalted is He, is greater than that His messenger should be a human like Muhammad, peace be upon him.' So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them﴾, the verse, and His statement, exalted is He: ﴿We did not send before you except men﴾, the verse." 

[p. 62]

When Allah, glorified is He, repeated the proofs against them, they said: "If he is a human, then someone other than Muhammad (ﷺ) would have been more deserving of prophethood. Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed in refutation of them: ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord?﴾, the verse. From this it is known that what is related in the second interpretation was the occasion of the revelation of another verse: ﴿that warn mankind﴾, meaning, inform them of what contains a warning for them about what results from doing what is not fitting. The intended meaning of "mankind" here is all people whom he, peace and blessings be upon him, is able to convey this to, not what was meant by "mankind" at first. This is the subtle reason for choosing the explicit noun over the pronoun. That the second is identical with the first when the definite noun is repeated is not absolute. The "that" (an) here is the one explaining the implied object of revelation, and what has the meaning of speech without its letters has preceded it, namely the revelation. Or it is the lightened form of the heavy "that," with its subject being the pronoun of the matter, and the imperative sentence as its predicate. There is disagreement over whether it may occur as the predicate of the pronoun of the matter without interpretation and without implying a word such as "saying." The author of al-Kashf held that this is not needed, because what is intended by it is explanation, and more than one scholar disagreed with him in this and held that there is no difference between its predicate and the predicate of anything else.

Some of them said: it is the verbal "that" (al-maṣdariyyah) which is light in its formation, based on the view that it connects to the imperative and the prohibition, while most scholars prohibit this. Abu Hayyan mentioned this possibility here, although it is reported from him in al-Mughni that his position is prohibition, because the meaning of the imperative is lost when it is made into a verbal noun.

واعْتُرِضَ بِأنَّهُ يُفَوِّتُ مَعْنى المُضِيِّ والحالِيَّةِ والِاسْتِقْبالِ المَقْصُودَ أيْضًا مَعَ الِاتِّفاقِ عَلى جَوازِ وصْلِها بِما يَدُلُّ عَلى ذَلِكَ. وأُجِيبَ بِأنَّهُ قَدْ يُقالُ: إنَّ بَيْنَهُما فَرْقًا، فَإنَّ المَصْدَرَ يَدُلُّ عَلى الزَّمانِ التِزامًا، فَقَدْ تُنْصَبُ عَلَيْهِ قَرِينَةٌ، فَلا يَفُوتُ مَعْناهُ بِالكُلِّيَّةِ، بِخِلافِ الأمْرِ والنَّهْيِ، فَإنَّهُ لا دَلالَةَ لِلْمَصْدَرِ عَلَيْهِما أصْلًا. وقالَ بَعْضُ المُدَقِّقِينَ: إنَّ المَصْدَرَ كَما يَجُوزُ أخْذُهُ مِن جَوْهَرِ الكَلِمَةِ يَجُوزُ أخْذُهُ مِنَ الهَيْئَةِ وما يُتْبِعُها، فَيُقَدَّرُ في هَذا ونَحْوِهِ: أوْحَيْنا إلَيْهِ الأمْرَ بِالإنْذارِ، كَما قُدِّرَ في ﴿أنْ لا تَزْنِي خَيْرٌ﴾: عَدَمُ الزِّنا خَيْرٌ. ولا يَخْفى أنَّ هَذا البَحْثَ يَجْرِي في (أنِ) المُخَفَّفَةِ مِنَ الثَّقِيلَةِ، لِأنَّها مَصْدَرِيَّةٌ أيْضًا، وإنَّ أقَلَّ الِاحْتِمالاتِ مُؤْنَةً احْتِمالُ التَّفْسِيرِ.

﴿وبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ بِما أوْحَيْناهُ إلَيْكَ وصَدَّقُوهُ ﴿أنَّ لَهُمْ﴾ أيْ بِأنَّ لَهُمْ ﴿قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ﴾ أيْ سابِقَةً ومَنزِلَةً رَفِيعَةً ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾. وأصْلُ القَدَمِ العُضْوُ المَخْصُوصُ، وأُطْلِقَتْ عَلى السَّبَقِ مَجازًا مُرْسَلًا (أي مَجازًا بِعَلاقَةٍ غَيْرِ المُشابَهَةِ، وهو المَجازُ المُرْسَلُ) لِكَوْنِها سَبَبَهُ وآلَتَهُ، وأُرِيدَ مِنَ السَّبْقِ الفَضْلُ والشَّرَفُ والتَّقَدُّمُ المَعْنَوِيُّ إلى المَنازِلِ الرَّفِيعَةِ مَجازًا أيْضًا، فالمَجازُ هُنا بِمَرْتَبَتَيْنِ. وقِيلَ: المُرادُ تَقَدُّمُهم عَلى غَيْرِهِمْ في دُخُولِ الجَنَّةِ، لِقَوْلِهِ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ: «نَحْنُ الآخِرُونَ السّابِقُونَ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ»، وقَوْلِهِ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ: «إنَّ الجَنَّةَ مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلى الأنْبِياءِ حَتّى أدْخُلَها أنا، وعَلى الأُمَمِ حَتّى تَدْخُلَها أُمَّتِي». وقِيلَ: تَقَدُّمُهم في البَعْثِ.

وأصْلُ الصِّدْقِ ما يَكُونُ في الأقْوالِ، ويُسْتَعْمَلُ كَما قالَ الرّاغِبُ في الأفْعالِ، فَيُقالُ: صَدَقَ في القِتالِ إذا وفّاهُ حَقَّهُ، وكَذا في ضِدِّهِ يُقالُ: كَذَبَ فِيهِ، فَيُعَبَّرُ بِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ فِعْلٍ فاضِلٍ ظاهِرًا وباطِنًا، ويُضافُ إلَيْهِ كَمَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ ومَدْخَلِ صِدْقٍ ومُخْرَجِ صِدْقٍ إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ. وصَرَّحُوا هُنا بِأنَّ الإضافَةَ مِن إضافَةِ المَوْصُوفِ إلى صِفَتِهِ، والأصْلُ: قَدَمُ صِدْقٍ، أيْ مُحَقَّقَةٌ مُقَرَّرَةٌ، وفِيهِ مُبالَغَةٌ لِجَعْلِها عَيْنَ الصِّدْقِ، ثُمَّ جَعْلِ الصِّدْقِ كَأنَّهُ صاحِبُها. ويَحْتَمِلُ أنْ تَكُونَ الإضافَةُ مِن إضافَةِ المُسَبِّبِ إلى السَّبَبِ، وفي ذَلِكَ تَنْبِيهٌ عَلى أنَّ ما نالُوهُ مِنَ المَنازِلِ الرَّفِيعَةِ كانَ بِسَبَبِ صِدْقِ القَوْلِ والنِّيَّةِ.

وقالَ بَعْضُهم: إنَّ هَذا التَّنْبِيهَ قَدْ يَحْصُلُ عَلى الِاعْتِبارِ الأوَّلِ، لِأنَّ الصِّدْقَ قَدْ تُجُوِّزَ بِهِ عَنْ تَوْفِيَةِ الأُمُورِ الفاضِلَةِ حَقَّها، لِلُزُومِ الصِّدْقِ لَها حَتّى كَأنَّها تُوجَدُ بِدُونِهِ، ويَكْفِي مِثْلُهُ في ذَلِكَ التَّنْبِيهِ. وهَذا كَما قالُوا: إنَّ أبا لَهَبٍ يُشِيرُ إلى أنَّهُ جَهَنَّمِيٌّ، وفِيهِ خَفاءٌ كَما لا يَخْفى. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يُرادَ بِالقَدَمِ المَقامُ، بِإطْلاقِ الحالِ وإرادَةِ المَحَلِّ. وعَنِ الأزْهَرِيِّ أنَّ القَدَمَ: الشَّيْءُ الَّذِي تُقَدِّمُهُ قُدّامَكَ لِيَكُونَ عُدَّةً لَكَ حِينَ تُقْدِمُ عَلَيْهِ، ويُشْعِرُ بِأنَّهُ اسْمُ مَفْعُولٍ، وبِهِ صَرَّحَ بَعْضُهم، وقالَ: إنَّهُ كالنَّقْضِ. وقِيلَ: إنَّهُ اسْمٌ لِلْحُسْنى مِنَ العَبْدِ، كَما أنَّ اليَدَ اسْمٌ لِلْحُسْنى مِنَ السَّيِّدِ، وفَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَ العَبْدِ والسَّيِّدِ، وهو مِنَ الغَرابَةِ بِمَكانٍ، ولا يَكادُ يَصِحُّ في قَوْلِ ذِي الرُّمَّةِ:

لَكُمْ قَدَمٌ لا يُنْكِرُ النّاسُ أنَّها ∗∗∗ مَعَ الحَسَبِ العادِيِّ طَمَتْ عَلى البَحْرِ

وقَوْلِهِ:

وأنْتَ امْرُؤٌ مِن أهْلِ بَيْتِ ذُؤابَةٍ ∗∗∗ لَهُمْ قَدَمٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ في المَفاخِرِ

والسَّبْقُ هو الأسْبَقُ إلى الذِّهْنِ في ذَلِكَ، وكَذا في قَوْلِ حَسّانَ:

لَنا القَدَمُ العُلْيا إلَيْكَ وخَلْفَنا ∗∗∗ لِأوَّلِنا في طاعَةِ اللَّهِ تابِعُ

(وقَوْلِ الآخَرِ)

صَلِّ لِذِي العَرْشِ واتَّخِذْ قَدَمًا ∗∗∗ تُنْجِيكَ يَوْمَ العِثارِ والزَّلَلِ

مُحْتَمِلٌ لِسائِرِ المَعانِي. وهَلْ يُطْلَقُ عَلى سابِقَةِ السُّوءِ أوْ لا؟ الظّاهِرُ الأوَّلُ، وقَدْ نَصَّ عَلى ذَلِكَ أبُو عُبَيْدَةَ والكِسائِيُّ.

وقالَ صاحِبُ الِانْتِصافِ: لَمْ يُسَمُّوا سابِقَةَ السُّوءِ قَدَمًا، إمّا لِكَوْنِ المَجازِ لا يَطَّرِدُ، وإمّا لِأنَّهُ غَلَبَ في العُرْفِ عَلى سابِقَةِ الخَيْرِ، وفِيهِ نَظَرٌ. وتَفْسِيرُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ تَعالى عَنْهُما لَهُ بِالأجْرِ، وابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ بِالعَمَلِ، لا يَخْرُجُ عَمّا ذَكَرْنا مِن مَعانِيهِ، وكَذا تَفْسِيرُ عَلِيٍّ كَرَّمَ اللَّهُ تَعالى وجْهَهُ، وأبِي سَعِيدٍ الخُدْرِيِّ والحَسَنِ وزَيْدِ بْنِ أسْلَمَ، لَهُ بِرَأْسِ المَوْجُوداتِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ، يَرْجِعُ إلى تَفْسِيرِهِ بِالخَيْرِ والسَّعادَةِ، كَما قالَهُ جَمْعٌ، وكَوْنُهُ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ خَيْرًا وسَعادَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِمّا لا يَمْتَرِي فِيهِ مُؤْمِنٌ. أوْ يُقالُ: إنَّ المُرادَ شَفاعَتُهُ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ، والأمْرُ في ذَلِكَ حِينَئِذٍ في غايَةِ الظُّهُورِ.

وخُصَّ التَّبْشِيرُ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ، لِأنَّهُ لا يَتَعَلَّقُ بِالكَفّارِ، وتَبْشِيرُهم إنْ آمَنُوا راجِعٌ إلى تَبْشِيرِ المُؤْمِنِينَ. وهَذا بِخِلافِ الإنْذارِ، فَإنَّهُ يَتَعَلَّقُ بِالمُؤْمِنِ والكافِرِ، ولِذَلِكَ ذَكَرَهُ سُبْحانَهُ، ولَمْ يَذْكُرْ جَلَّ وعَلا المُنْذَرَ بِهِ لِلتَّعْمِيمِ والتَّهْوِيلِ، وذَكَرَ المُبَشَّرَ بِهِ عَلى الوَجْهِ الَّذِي ذَكَرَهُ لِتَقْوى رَغْبَةُ المُؤْمِنِينَ فِيما يُؤَدِّيهِمْ إلَيْهِ. وقَدَّمَ الإنْذارَ عَلى التَّبْشِيرِ، لِأنَّ التَّخْلِيَةَ مُقَدَّمَةٌ عَلى التَّحْلِيَةِ، وإزالَةَ ما لا يَنْبَغِي مُقَدَّمَةٌ في الرُّتْبَةِ عَلى فِعْلِ ما يَنْبَغِي.

﴿قالَ الكافِرُونَ﴾ هُمُ المُتَعَجِّبُونَ، وإيرادُهم بِهَذا العُنْوانِ عَلى بابِهِ، وتَرْكُ العاطِفِ لِجَرَيانِهِ مَجْرى البَيانِ لِلْجُمْلَةِ الَّتِي دَخَلَ عَلَيْها هَمْزَةُ الإنْكارِ، أوْ لِكَوْنِهِ اسْتِئْنافًا مَبْنِيًّا عَلى السُّؤالِ، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: ماذا صَنَعُوا بَعْدَ التَّعَجُّبِ؟ هَلْ بَقُوا عَلى التَّرَدُّدِ والِاسْتِبْعادِ، أوْ قَطَعُوا فِيهِ بِشَيْءٍ؟ فَقِيلَ: قالَ الكافِرُونَ عَلى طَرِيقَةِ التَّأْكِيدِ ﴿إنَّ هَذا﴾ أيْ ما أُوحِيَ إلَيْهِ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ مِنَ الكِتابِ المُنْطَوِي عَلى الإنْذارِ والتَّبْشِيرِ. وزَعَمَ الخازِنُ أنَّ في الكَلامِ حَذْفًا، أيْ: أكانَ لِلنّاسِ عَجَبًا أنْ أوْحَيْنا إلى رَجُلٍ مِنهم أنْ أنْذِرْ وبَشِّرْ؟ فَلَمّا جاءَهم بِالوَحْيِ وأنْذَرَهم قالَ الكافِرُونَ: إنَّ هَذا ﴿لَساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ 2، أيْ ظاهِرٌ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ والكُوفِيُّونَ (لَساحِرٌ) عَلى أنَّ الإشارَةَ إلى رَجُلٍ، وعَنَوْا بِهِ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلّى اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِ وسَلَّمَ. وفي قِراءَةِ أُبَيٍّ: (ما هَذا إلّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ)، وأرادُوا بِالسِّحْرِ الحاصِلَ بِالمَصْدَرِ. وفي هَذا اعْتِرافٌ بِأنَّ ما عايَنُوهُ خارِجٌ عَنْ طَوْقِ البَشَرِ، نازِلٌ مِن حَضْرَةِ خَلّاقِ القُوى والقَدَرِ، ولَكِنَّهم يُسَمُّونَهُ بِما قالُوا تَمادِيًا في العِنادِ، كَما هو شَنْشَنَةُ المُكابِرِ اللَّجُوجِ ونَشْنَشَةُ المُفْحَمِ المَحْجُوجِ.

[p. 65]

﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾ is a resumptive statement (isti'naf), brought to demonstrate the falsehood of the astonishment mentioned above and of the false claim that followed it, after pointing out that they regarded it with denial and wonder. In it, the truth of what they marvelled at and the correctness of what they denied are established by a general indication of some of the matters that point to it, namely the affairs of creation and decree and the states of origination and governance. It guides them to knowledge of these matters with the slightest reminder, since they acknowledge it without objection, as is shown by more than one verse of the Noble Book. The emphasis (ta'kid) is for greater attention to the content of the sentence, according to what is apparent. That is: your Lord and the Owner of your affairs, at whom you marvel that He should send to you a man from among you with warning and good tidings, and whose revelation of the Book you consider to be magic, is ﴿Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, that is, periods of time. So "day" here is taken in its linguistic sense, which is any period of time. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that those days are among the days of the Hereafter, one day of which is like a thousand years of what you count. It has also been said that they are the length of six days of this world, and this is the more suitable to the context, because it indicates the overwhelming power in creating these great bodies within such a short period, and because it is a description (ta'rif) for us in terms of what we know. The day cannot be understood as the familiar day, because, as it has been said, it is the expression of the sun being above the earth, and this cannot be conceived of when there is no earth and no heaven. The day in this sense is called the single daylight (al-nahar al-mufrad), and "day" is also applied to the whole of that daylight together with its night. The length of that period is then possibly intended here too. Some of the eminent scholars have stated that by "the heavens" is meant all of them except the outermost sphere (al-muhaddad, the sphere that encloses and limits the others, in their terminology), and that "day" here is the expression for the duration of one complete revolution of that sphere. It should not be hidden that the linguistic meaning of "day" also includes this, but its intended use, like the intended use of the length of the whole of a daylight and its night, requires a transmission (naql), and this is not a matter known to the addressees so as to dispense with transmission. Moreover, this view depends on the outermost sphere having a diurnal motion (al-harakah al-wad'iyyah), and that too requires transmission. Likewise it depends on the outermost sphere being outside the heavens created in the six days, yet this does no harm, since the verses and reports bear witness to its being outside, as is not hidden. In creating them successively, although He has complete power to originate them in the twinkling of an eye, there is a lesson for observers and an exhortation for them to be deliberate regarding states and stages. There is also in it, as some verifying scholars have stated, a proof of choice (ikhtiyar). As for specifying this number, it has been said that it is a matter for which the Knower of the unseen has kept to Himself the knowledge of what it requires, may His power be exalted and His wisdom be subtle. It has also been said that He, glory be to Him, appointed for each of the creation of the material of the heavens and their forms, and the joining of some of them to others, and the creation of the material of the earth and its form, and the joining of one of them to the other, a time, and therefore the times became six. In this there is room for reflection. The verification of this matter, in a manner by which the dust is cleared from the insight of the observers, will come in the commentary on surah al-Dukhan, if Allah the Exalted wills.

The choice of the plural form "heavens", as is well known, signals that they are bodies differing in natures and distinct in effects and rulings. Their being mentioned before the earth is either because they are greater in creation, or because they function as the agent while the earth functions as the receiver, as has been explained in its proper place. The earth is mentioned before them in the verse of Ta-Ha because it is closer to the senses and more evident to them, and its verification will also come there, if Allah the Exalted wills. ﴿Then He settled Himself upon the Throne﴾, in the sense that He, glory be to Him, intended, without asking how (kayf); the modality (kayf) is withheld. It has been said that settling upon the Throne is a metaphor for kingship and sovereignty, derived from the figure of speech (kinayah) concerning one for whom sitting on a throne is possible; one says: so-and-so settled upon the throne of kingship, and what is meant is his rule, even if he never sits on the throne at all. It has also been said that settling (al-istiwa') means taking control (al-istila'), and they referred it to the attribute of power. You know that this and similar expressions belong to the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters, and people have various positions concerning them.

[p. 66]

What we have pointed to is the view of most of the early generations of the Community (salaf al-ummah), may Allah be pleased with them. Some have stated that settling is an attribute other than the eight attributes, whose reality no one knows except the One to whom it belongs, and that inability to grasp the grasping is itself a grasping. Many of the later generations (khalaf) chose that what is meant by it is kingship and sovereignty, and mentioned it to show the greatness of His kingship and sovereignty, glory be to Him, after showing the greatness of His majesty and the vastness of His power through the creation of those great bodies mentioned earlier. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿He manages the affair﴾ is a resumptive statement, showing the wisdom of His settling upon the Throne, may He be majestic and exalted, and establishing His greatness. Tadbir (management) in the language means looking at the outcomes and consequences of affairs so that they fall in the praiseworthy manner. What is meant by it here is the decree that proceeds in accordance with wisdom and in the most perfect and complete manner. Abu al-Shaykh and others reported from Mujahid that the meaning is "He decrees the affair", and by "the affair" is meant the affair of the existents, upper and lower, even the Throne, so the definite article in it is for previous reference, that is, He decrees the affair of all of that in the most excellent way and the fitting pattern, according to what the public good requires and wisdom demands. What they marvelled at is included in what has been mentioned, clearly. Some claimed that the meaning is: He manages that in accordance with what His wisdom requires, and prepares its causes through the motion of the Throne, which in their view is the sphere of spheres (falak al-aflak), and by its motion the other spheres, the planetary and others, are moved, by the strength of its own nature. It has also been said that this is because all of them are within it, so the motion of the container entails the motion of what is contained, and this is based on the view that the container is the natural place of what is contained; otherwise there is room for scrutiny. You know that this kind of claim, with what is in it, is not accepted by the later scholars (al-muhdathun) or by the early generations of the Community, since neither the Book nor the Sunnah bears witness to it. Accordingly, no legal ruling is to be given on its basis, even if a judge has decided on it.

It has been permitted in general that this sentence be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "settled", and that it be in the nominative position as a second predicate of "inna". In any case, the choice of the imperfect form signals the renewal of management and its continuance from Him, exalted be He. His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ is a statement of His sole authority in management and decree, and a negation of intercession in the most emphatic way, since the negation of all individual intercessors with the exclusive "min" (min al-istighraqiyyah) entails the negation of intercession in the fullest sense. So there is no need to say that the sense is: there is no intercession for any intercessor. In it there is also a further establishing of His greatness, glory be to Him, following a previous establishing. The exception is an exception from the most general of times, that is: there is no intercessor who intercedes for anyone at any time except after His permission, exalted be He, which is founded on overwhelming wisdom. This applies when the intercessor is one of the chosen and righteous, and the one interceded for is one who is worthy of intercession. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) held that in it there is a refutation of those who claim that their gods intercede for them with Allah, exalted be He.

It has been objected that this is not complete, because when they claimed the intercession of these gods, they might also claim permission for them, so how is this refutation complete? And there is no indication in the verse that they will not be given permission. As for what has been said, that this is an unsupported claim and that supposing it is useless and has no benefit, except if it is said that its intent is that idols do not perceive and do not speak, so that their being in a position to be given permission is obviously not part of their nature. His saying, exalted be His glory: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ is a resumptive statement for further establishing and emphasis in admonition, and as a consequence (tafri') of the command to worship, expressed in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿So worship Him﴾. The demonstrative refers to the Essence described by those attributes which necessitate deserving what is reported about Him, and that Essence is Allah, and "your Lord", for both are predicates of "that". Since the reason for this being established for Him is what has been mentioned, which is not found in anyone else, it requires its being restricted to Him, and it signifies that there is no lord other than Him and no worshipped one besides Him. It is also permissible that the august name be an adjective (na't) for the demonstrative, with "your Lord" as its predicate, or that it be the predicate with "your Lord" as an appositive (bayan) or a substitute (badal) for it. In any case the sentence conveys restriction (inhisar). When the command mentioned is consequent upon this, it conveys the command to worship Him alone, glory be to Him, that is: worship Him, glory be to Him, without associating with Him anything, whether an angel or a prophet, let alone an inanimate object that neither sees nor hears, nor harms nor benefits. What prompts this reading is not that the basic act of worship belongs to them, so that the command to it is taken in that sense to be beneficial, as some have said, that the address is to the polytheists, and there is no worship together with polytheism. ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾, that is: do you know that the matter is as has been detailed? Then you do not take heed of it, so that you would stand upon the corruption of what you are upon, and refrain from it, and worship Allah the Exalted alone. The choice of "take heed" (tadhakkarun) over "reflect" (tafakkarun) is to signal that the matter is manifest and as if known, requiring not complete reflection nor perfect examination, but merely a turning of attention and a bringing of it to mind.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 10, verse 4:

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾ is like a reason (ta'lil) for the obligation of worship. The prepositional phrase (al-jar wa al-majrur) is a predicate (khabar) placed before its subject, and ﴿your return﴾ (marji'ukum) is a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar). It is a mimi verbal noun (masdar mimi), not a noun of place (ism makan), contrary to those who have erred in this. ﴿All of you﴾ (jami'an) is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the pronoun in the genitive, because it is the doer in meaning. That is: your return to Him, the Exalted, is as a gathered body, not to other than Him, glorified is He, by resurrection. ﴿A promise of God﴾ (wa'da Allah) is an absolute infinitive (masdar mu'akkid) emphasizing the content of the preceding sentence, because it is a promise from Him, exalted is He, of resurrection. Since it admits of no meaning other than promise, this is among the instances of the absolute infinitive that emphasizes itself (al-mu'akkid li-nafsihi) according to them, as in your saying: "He owes me a thousand by custom" (lahu 'alayya alf 'urfan). It may also be in the accusative as an infinitive of a verb omitted, meaning: God promised a promise (wa'ada Allahu wa'dan). In either case, this is evidence that the intended meaning of "return" is the return by resurrection, because the return by death has no connection with the promise, just as it has no connection with gathering. Therefore what occurs in some copies of al-Qadi, "by death or by rising (al-nushur)," is not as it should be.

And ﴿A promise of God﴾ has been read in the verbal form with the sacred Name in the nominative as the agent (fa'iliyyah). ﴿Truly (haqqan)﴾ is an absolute infinitive emphasizing what the first (verb) indicates, and it belongs to the category of the absolute infinitive that emphasizes something other than itself (al-mu'akkid li-ghayrihi), because the first is not explicit in it, since a promise admits of both truth and failure. It has been said that it is accusative by "promised" (wa'ada) with an implied "in" (fi), and its resemblance to an adverb of time or place is like his saying: "Is it true that I am besotted, enamoured with you?" (afi al-haqqi anniha'imun bika mughramun).

The first is more apparent.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed He originates creation, then repeats it﴾ is like a reason for what ﴿To Him is your return﴾ conveys, for the ultimate purpose of origination and repetition is recompense in accordance with what is fitting. Abu Ja'far and al-A'mash read (annahu) with a fatha on the hamza, on the estimate of (li-annahu, "because He"). It is also permitted that it be accusative by the same thing that made (wa'da) accusative, meaning: God, glorified is He, promised the origination of creation and then its repetition, that is, its repetition after its origination. The promise then falls on the whole, but with regard to the last part, since the origination is not what was promised. It is also permitted that it be nominative by the same thing that made (haqqan) accusative, meaning: the origination of creation and then its repetition are true (haqqa bad'u al-khalqi thumma i'aduhu). This is like the verse of al-Hamasi:

Is it true, servants of God, that I shall not see Rifa'a all the length of time, except in imagination?

From al-Marzuqi it is reported that he parsed it as accusative in the sense of time (zarfiyyah), and it is either a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam) or a relied-upon adverb (zarf mu'tamad). It has been claimed that this is the school of Sibawayh. It is also permitted that the accusative be by "God's promise" as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), and the nominative by "truly" as its agent. The apparent sense of the words of al-Kashshaf indicates that the two verbs governing the two mentioned infinitives are the ones that govern what has been mentioned, not two other verbs like them. In that case the matter of emphasis that we mentioned is lost, because the agent of a verb governing an emphasized infinitive must refer back to what preceded it that it emphasizes.

It has been read: (It is true that He originates creation), and it is like your saying: "It is true that Zayd is departing." It has been read: (yubdi'u), from abda'a. Perhaps what is meant by "creation" is such as the responsible beings (mukallafin), not what includes that and inanimate things. What supports this is what many have reported from Mujahid, that the meaning of the verse is: He gives life to creation, then causes it to die, then gives it life again.

﴿That He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾: that is, with justice (bil-qist, bil-'adl). It is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the doer of (yajza, "He recompenses"), meaning: while being clothed in justice. Or it is connected to (yajza): that He may recompense them by His justice and grant them their rewards. Page 67 Rewards are only summarily stated here to signal that a restricted enumeration cannot exhaust it. This is reinforced by making His noble Essence itself the one who recompenses, or (bi-qistihim) by their own equity and justice in their affairs, or by their faith. This last is preferred, on the ground that it better suits His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment, because of what they used to disbelieve﴾ (4). For its meaning is: He recompenses those who disbelieved with a drink of hot water whose heat has reached its extreme, and a painful punishment because of their disbelief. Thus the antithesis between the causes of the recompense of believers and the recompense of disbelievers becomes evident, although there is no reason to restrict justice to the recompense of believers; rather the recompense of the others is more deserving of it, as is clear. The repetition of the predication, by making the verbal sentence a predicate of the relative pronoun, is for strengthening the ruling. The combination of the two forms, the past and the present, is to indicate their persistence in disbelief. The alteration of the noble structure is for exaggeration regarding their deserving of punishment, by making it an established truth for them, and to signal that torment is far from being included in the chain of the final cause of the repetition, according to the connection of (li-yajza) to the first part, and of the origination according to its connection to both, by way of dispute (tanazu'). What is included in that chain is only reward, so it is the one intended in itself, while punishment occurs incidentally.

[p. 68 begins at the midpoint, see below]

﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance﴾ is an alert to inferring His existence, oneness, knowledge, power, and wisdom from the traces of His handiwork in the two luminaries, after the alert to inferring by what has passed, and an explanation of some of the instances of the governance that was indicated in a general way, and a guidance that when He, glorified is He, governed their affairs related to their livelihood with this wondrous governance, then it is more fitting and more appropriate that He govern their interests related to their final return by sending the Messengers and sending down the Books. Or, "made" is either in the sense of "created and originated," so that *ḍiyā'an* (radiance) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) from its object, or it is in the sense of "rendered," so that it is its second object, and the speech is in the manner of "the narrowness of the mouth of the waterskin," since the sun was not devoid of that state. It is said that the word is taken from *shimsat al-qilāda* (the central large bead of a necklace), and it was named thus because it is the greatest of the stars, as the traces indicate and the senses bear witness. This is the view of the majority of the astronomers (*ahl al-hay'a*, the specialists in celestial configuration). Some said: it was named thus because it is in the middle sphere (*falak*) among the spheres, between the upper spheres and the three other lower ones. This is a speculative matter, which the prophetic reports do not confirm, as you will learn shortly, God willing. *Ḍiyā'* is a verbal noun (maṣdar) like *qiyām*. Abu 'Ali (al-Farisi) said in *al-Ḥujja*: its being a plural, like *ḥawḍ* and *ḥiyāḍ*, and *sawṭ* and *siyāṭ*, is more analogous than its being a verbal noun. It was objected that the singular *nūr* mentioned afterwards favours the first view. Its *yā'* is changed from a *wāw* because of the kasra before it. The original form of the speech is "made the sun possessing radiance."

It is permissible to make the verbal noun in the sense of an active participle, i.e., *muḍī'a* (shining), and to leave it on its apparent sense without an added term, so that it conveys emphasis by making her the very essence of radiance. Ibn Kathir recited *ḍi'ā'an* with two hamzas separated by an *alif*. The reasoning behind it, as Abu al-Baqa' said, is that the original is *ḍiyā'* with the *yā'* at the end, and the hamza was placed first. When the *yā'* came at the end after an extra *alif*, it was changed to a hamza according to some, and according to others it was changed to an *alif*, and then the *alif* was changed to a hamza so that two *alifs* would not come together.

﴿and the moon a light﴾: that is, possessing light, or illuminating, or the very essence of light, in the manner mentioned just before. *Nūr* (light) is said to be more general than *ḍaw'* (radiance), on the basis that *ḍaw'* is what is strong among light, whereas *nūr* covers both the strong and the weak.

The intended meaning of His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ is the comparison of His guidance, which He set up for people, to the light present at night during darkness. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, placed His guidance like light in darkness, so some are guided and others go astray. Had He made it like the radiance that leaves no darkness with it, no one would have gone astray, and that contradicts wisdom. But there is a question about this. It was also said: the two are distinct, so what is essential is radiance (*ḍiyā'*), and what is derivative is light (*nūr*). Because the sun is luminous in itself, radiance is attributed to it, and because the moon's light is derived from it, light is attributed to it. The second Allama criticised this, saying that this is the view of the philosophers (*ḥukamā'*) and has nothing to do with the language, for the expression "the light of the sun" and "the light of the fire" is widespread.

We have already extensively discussed this matter earlier and in our book *al-Ṭirāz al-Mudhhab*, and we have given therein a guidance for those who reflect.

There remains the matter of the derivation mentioned, whether it is by way of reflection without the moon's substance becoming luminous, as in a mirror, or by its substance becoming luminous, which is more probable according to the Imam. Many people have mentioned it, even al-Qadi in his commentary. It is among matters that did not come in any report from the one who ascended to heaven, ﷺ. It came only from the philosophers. They claimed that the total spheres are nine: the highest is the sphere of spheres, then the sphere of the fixed stars, then the sphere of Kayvan (Saturn), then the sphere of Birjis (Jupiter), then the sphere of Bahram (Mars), then the sphere of the sun, then the sphere of Venus, then the sphere of Mercury, then the sphere of the moon. The author of *al-Tuḥfa* claimed that the sphere of the sun is below the sphere of Venus. What the majority hold is the first arrangement. Many of them argued for this order from what leaves room for confusion between the sun and Venus and Mercury, such as eclipses (*kasf*) and occultations (*inkisāf*), and the variation in aspect known through the instrument with two arms (*dhāt al-shu'batayn*). The first cannot be imagined there, because Venus and Mercury burn up at conjunction in most of the inhabited world. The second is also impossible for that instrument, because it is set up in the plane of the midday meridian, and these two planets do not appear there, since they are within less than two signs of the sun. When they reach midday, the sun is above the earth to the east or west, so they are not seen at all.

The placing of the sun in the middle sphere was for the beauty of the arrangement, as if it were the central bead of a necklace, or because it holds the position of a king in the world. Just as it is fitting for a king to be in the middle of the army, so it is fitting for her to be in the middle of the spheres of the world. This is a persuasive argument, rather it is of the kind of clinging to the mountains of the moon (i.e., attempting the impossible). Similar to this is their argument against adding more spheres beyond these, saying there is no superiority in celestial matters. Yet it follows from this that the thickness of the greatest sphere would be the least thickness possible for bodies, since there is no star in it, so that its thickness would be equal to its diameter. What exceeds the least possible is a superiority. It has been made clear in the treatise on *al-Abʿād wa-al-Ajrām* (Distances and Bodies) that it reached the limit in thickness, and we have already set this out for you. At that point, it is possible that each of the fixed stars has its own separate sphere, and that those spheres agree in their movements in direction, pole, zodiacal belt, and speed. Indeed, if it were said that some of them differ, there would be no proof to negate it, because what has been observed of them is a very small amount. So it is possible that some of what has not been observed differs. Moreover, some people have affirmed a sphere above the sphere of the fixed stars and below the greatest sphere, and they argued for it with what has been argued. Whoever knows that the astronomers, in a short time, found a planet slower in motion than Saturn and named it Herschel, and Lalande observed it and found that it crosses a sign in six solar years, eleven months, and twenty-seven days, and that is the day of our writing this discussion, namely the twenty-fourth of Jumada al-Akhira in the year 1256, when the sun is in Virgo, one degree and thirteen minutes have been crossed from Pisces, returning. There is no longer reliance on what the earlier scholars said. And similar discoveries achieved by these later scholars are possible.

Also, it is permissible that the spheres are eight, because it is not possible for all the fixed stars to be fixed in a convex surface representing Saturn, meaning in its enclosing completion, while it moves with the slow motion. The eighth sphere moves with the rapid motion, and then the circles of the zodiac passing through the beginnings of the signs are moved by the motion of the eighth, not moved by the motion of the representing sphere, so that the transfer of the fixed stars from sign to sign happens by the motion of the representing sphere, as is the reality. Al-Birjandi stated that the ancients did not affirm the greatest sphere, and that it was affirmed by the later scholars.

Also, it is permissible that they are seven, by supposing that the fixed stars and the circle of the zodiac are on the convex surface of the representing sphere of Saturn, and there are two souls there: one connected to the whole of the seven and moving them by the first two motions, and the other with the seventh sphere, moving it by the other motion. But on the condition that the circles of the zodiac are supposed to move by the rapid motion only, not the slow one, as they are imagined moving on the surfaces of the representations by the rapid motion alone, so that the fixed stars are carried by the slow motion from sign to sign, as is the reality. We stand back from prohibition regarding what refutes this possibility.

Also, the Imam mentioned: why is it not permissible that the fixed stars are beneath the sphere of the moon, so they would be beneath the spheres of the planets and not above them? As for what is said, that we see these planets eclipse the fixed stars, and the eclipsing body must necessarily be beneath the eclipsed, it is answered that these planets only eclipse the fixed stars near the zodiac belt, not those near the two poles. So why is it not permissible to say that those fixed stars near the zodiac belt are fixed in the eighth sphere, and those near the two poles are fixed in another sphere beneath the sphere of the moon? Moreover, why is it not permissible to say that the stars move by themselves without being fixed in another body? Without establishing the impossibility, it would be like pulling out thorns (*kharṭ al-qatād*), i.e., an unnecessary and fruitless struggle.

Regarding the derivation of the moon's light from the sun's radiance, they mentioned that it is among the conjectural matters, because its shapes vary according to its nearness and distance from it. As Ibn al-Haytham said, this does not establish certainty regarding the derivation, because it is possible that the moon is a sphere, half of which is luminous and half dark, and it rotates on its own axis, so it appears as a crescent, then full, then wanes, and so on always. His intention is that something else must be added to the variation of shapes according to nearness and distance, to prove the claim, namely the occurrence of eclipse when the earth comes between it and the sun. Some scholars, such as the author of *Ḥikmat al-ʿAyn* and the author of *al-Mawāqif*, transmitted what they transmitted from Ibn al-Haytham and did not grasp his intention from it. So they said: it is weak, otherwise the moon would never be eclipsed at any of its oppositions at all. Al-Amili said regarding that: it is strange from them, and you know that there is no certainty either, and that adding what was added is because it is possible that there is another cause for the variation of those luminous shapes which we do not know, such as a dark star beneath the sphere of the moon by which it is eclipsed at some of its conjunctions.

And if it is objected to this that if that were so, it would have been seen, we say: why is it not permissible that that variation and eclipse are the effects of the will of the free Agent, without the mediation of nearness and distance from the sun and the interposition of the earth between them? Rather there is nothing there except the mediation of *kāf* and *nūn* (i.e., "Be!"), and that is sufficient for one whose eye is free of the *ghayn* (the blindness of heedlessness). And for the legalists among the later scholars, and likewise for our masters the Sufis, may God sanctify their secrets, there are famous sayings on this matter. Perhaps you have already come across them, and if not, you will come across them later, God willing.

They relied, in what they say, on prophetic reports and inner observations. Most of the reports on this matter do not reach the degree of sound (*ṣaḥīḥ*), and what reaches some degree is only solitary (*āḥād*). Even so, it is open to interpretation in a way that does not contradict the doctrine of the philosophers. The truth is that there is no certainty in what they say regarding the arrangement of the upper bodies and what is connected with that. Affirming it does no harm to the religion unless it contradicts what is known to have come from the Prophet, ﷺ.

[p. 69]

This (is the end of the discussion). The moon was named *qamar* for its whiteness, as al-Jawhari said. He and others considered that it is called *qamar* only after three nights.

﴿And measured it﴾: that is, determined for it and prepared it. ﴿stations﴾: or he measured its course through stations. So *manāzil* is the object on the first reading, and on the second reading it is in the adverbial sense of place. It is permissible that "measured" means "made," the transitive with one object, and "stations" is a circumstantial accusative from its object, that is, made it and created it moving from place to place. And it is permissible that it means "made" in the transitive with two objects, that is, rendered it possessing stations. In any case, the pronoun refers to the moon. Its being specified with this measurement is because of the swiftness of its movement relative to the sun, and because its stations are known and perceptible, and because it is the basis of the Arab histories, and because the rulings of the Sharia are mostly tied to it. It is permissible that the pronoun refers to it and to the sun, by interpreting each of them. The stations are twenty-eight: al-Sharatān, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Haq'a, al-Han'a, al-Dhirāʿ, al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabha, al-Zubra, and al-Ṣarfa.

Al-Alusi, Ruh al-Ma'ani, on surah 10, verse 5 (part 2 of 2):

Al-'Uwa', al-Simak al-A'zal, al-'Ufara, al-Zaban, al-Iklil, al-Qalb, al-Shawla, al-Na'a'im, al-Balda, Sa'd al-Dhabih, Sa'd Bula', Sa'd al-Su'ud, Sa'd al-Akhbiya, Faragh al-Dalw al-Muqaddam, al-Faragh al-Mu'akhkhar, and Batn al-Hut. These are divided among the twelve well-known zodiacal signs (al-buruj), so each sign contains two lunar mansions and a third. According to them, a sign is thirty degrees, obtained by dividing the three hundred and sixty parts of the circle of the zodiac by twelve. A degree, according to them, is divided into sixty minutes (daqiqa), each minute into sixty seconds (thaniya), each second into sixty thirds (thalitha), and so on to the fourths, fifths, sixths, and others. The Moon, by its own motion, covers in each day with its night thirteen degrees, three minutes, fifty-three seconds, and fifty-six thirds. The naming of what we have mentioned as "mansions" is metaphorical, because it refers to particular fixed stars close to the ecliptic (al-minqata). The real station (al-manzila al-haqiqiyya) of the Moon is the space that the body of the Moon occupies, according to one of the opinions regarding place. Thus the meaning of the Moon's "descent" into those mansions is its being directly opposite them (musamatatuhu iyyaha). Likewise, the being directly opposite is considered in its descent into the signs, because they are first assumed in the greatest sphere (al-falak al-a'zam). As for naming the likes of Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), and Gemini (al-Jawza) by these names, it is also on the basis of being directly opposite.

The first of the mansions was al-Sharatayn, also called al-Natah, and it belongs to the beginning of Aries. Then it moved until its first became, according to what the verifying scholars among the later ones have determined, al-Faragh al-Mu'akhkhar. The fixed stars do not, according to the correct view, have a consistent motion, although it is slow; it is the motion of their sphere. Those who affirm this differed regarding the amount of time in which they traverse one unit of the degrees of their ecliptic. It is said to be sixty-six solar years or sixty-eight lunar years. Ibn al-A'lam held that it is seventy solar years, and the new observation undertaken by Nasir al-Din al-Tusi at Maragha agreed with him. Muhyi al-Din, one of his companions, claimed that he undertook the observation of a number of fixed stars, such as 'Ayn al-Thawr and Qalb al-'Aqrab, by that observation, and found them moving one degree every sixty-six solar years. Batlamyus (Ptolemy) claimed that he found the fixed stars close to the ecliptic moving one degree every hundred solar years. And God Most High knows the realities of the matters, and He is the Disposer of His dominion and His kingdom as He wills.

﴿That you may know the number of the years﴾, which is connected with a scientific purpose for establishing your religious and worldly interests. ﴿And the reckoning﴾, i.e., and that you may know the reckoning of times by months, days, and other things to which some of the mentioned interests are attached. The lam, according to what is understood from the Amali of 'Izz al-Din ibn 'Abd al-Salam, is connected to the verb "qaddara" (He determined). He himself raised an objection to this: the knowledge of number and reckoning does not require the Moon to be determined by mansions; rather, its rising and setting is sufficient. Some have mentioned that the wisdom in this is the good condition of fruits through the Moon's rays falling upon them gradually, and that it is more indicative of His existence, glorified and exalted be He, since the greater the variation in the states of the contingent and the greater the difference in its attributes, the more it calls for a wise Creator who is necessary in Himself. And other things that those acquainted with the secrets know. Our master Siri al-Din answered that what is meant by reckoning is the reckoning of times by knowing what has passed of the month and what remains of it, and likewise of the night. Then he said: this is when the lam is connected to "qaddara" as mansions; but if you connect it to "ja'ala" (He made) the sun and the moon, the question does not arise.

Perhaps the better course in this case is to take "al-sinin" (the years) to include both solar and lunar years, although the reckoning that counts in the Arab Islamic calendar is the lunar year. The difference between the two years is ten days, eleven hours, and one minute. The first year is three hundred and sixty-five days, five hours, and forty-nine minutes according to the Ablakhani observation, and the second year is three hundred and fifty-four days, eight hours, and forty-eight minutes; each of them is divided into a simple (basita) and an intercalary (kabisa) year. The explanation of this is in its proper place. The specification of number to years and of reckoning to times is because no distinct meaning was considered in the counted years beyond the levels of numbers, as was considered in the reckoned times. Its verification: reckoning is the enumeration of that which has quantity that is discrete, by repeating its like, such that a specific number of them results in a determinate number which has a special name and an independent judgment, like the year which results from twelve months, each of which results from known days, each of which results from hours likewise. Counting is merely the enumeration of it by repeating its like, without considering that something of that kind results from it. Since in the counted years there was no consideration of achieving a determinate limit that has a special name other than the names of the levels of numbers and an independent judgment, the number is attached to them; and the attainment of the levels of numbers, such as tens, hundreds, and thousands, is conventional and does not profit in achieving the counted thing. Where in the reckoned times the attainment of the mentioned levels, which have special names and independent judgments, was considered, the reckoning indicating that was attached to them. The year, in terms of its existence in itself, is something to which reckoning relates; what counting relates to is a portion of it, and its relation within that to each of that portion is not from the mentioned aspect, namely the aspect of its being achieved from a number of months, each of which is achieved from a number of days, each of which is achieved from a number of hours. That is the function of reckoning. Rather, it is from the aspect that it is a single unit of that counted portion, without any other thing being considered along with it.

The placing of number before reckoning, although the order between their objects in existence and in knowledge is the reverse, is because the knowledge related to the number of years has a general knowledge of what reckoning relates to in detail, even if the aspect is not unified; or because number, insofar as no achieving of another matter was considered in it, as verified just above, is treated, relative to the reckoning in which that was considered, as the simple relative to the compound. This was said by Shaykh al-Islam.

﴿God did not create that﴾, i.e., what was mentioned of the sun and the moon in the states God Most High described, ﴿except with truth﴾. This is an exception from the most general states of the agent and the object, and the ba' is for accompaniment: i.e., He did not create that accompanied by anything among things except accompanied by the truth, taking wisdom and benefit into account in it, or with that being taken into account in it. So what is meant by "truth" here is the opposite of falsehood and futility. ﴿He details the signs﴾, i.e., the cosmic signs mentioned, or more general than them, and what is mentioned enters primarily; or we detail the revealed signs that alert to that. It is read "nufassilu" with the plural of majesty, and there is a shift (iltifat) in it. ﴿For a people who know﴾ the wisdom in the origination of beings, so that they may infer by that the affairs of their Originator, exalted be He; or who know what is within the folds of the revealed signs, so that they believe in them.

The specification of the detailing to them according to both possibilities is because they are the ones who benefit from it. The intended meaning is "a people" of rational beings possessing knowledge, so it includes those we have mentioned and others.

Verse 6: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾ is another general admonition concerning what was mentioned, i.e., in their succession and in each of them being a replacement (khilfah) for the other, according to the rising and setting of the sun, which, according to most of the philosophers (falasifah), follow from the motion of the greatest sphere (al-falak al-a'zam) around its center in the opposite direction of the succession (al-tawali). For this motion necessitates the motion of all the other spheres and the stars within them, as has been explained earlier, while the earth remains at rest. This holds in most places. As for at latitude ninety, nothing rises or sets by that motion at all, but by other motions. Likewise, in places near to it, rising and setting may occur by other than that motion. That motion is called the daily motion (al-harakah al-yawmiyyah). Some have attributed all of it to the earth, and others have attributed part of it to the earth and part to the greatest sphere. The well-known view among many of the modern scholars (al-muhdathun) is that the sun itself runs, subjected by God's leave, in a restrained sea, so it rises and sets wherever God Most High wills.
Page 72
There is no motion of the heaven. To this same view went the Greatest Shaykh (al-Shaykh al-Akbar), may God sanctify his secret.

It is also possible that by the alternation of the night and the day is meant their differing in themselves: each of them increases as the other decreases, and decreases as the other increases. According to them, this arises from the variation in the sun's state relative to us in nearness and distance, because of its second motion, by which the seasons vary and the year is divided into seasons. Night and day may sometimes be equal for some people at certain times, and this happens only when the sun arrives at the point of equinox (nuqtat al-i'tidal) at sunrise or sunset, and the apogee (al-awj) is at one of the two equinoxes. When the first occurs, the arc of day is like the arc of night; when the second occurs, the situation is reversed. This is very rare. According to the view of Ptolemy (Batlamyus) that the apogee does not move, it is impossible, so night and day are never equal for him at all. It may also be meant that their difference is according to places. As for length and shortness, the lands near the North Pole have longer summer days and shorter summer nights than the lands far from it. As for their intrinsic nature, the sphericity of the earth, as they say, requires that at some times in some places it is night while in the opposite place it is day.

﴿And what God has created in the heavens and the earth﴾ of well-made creations and firmly established signs ﴿are signs﴾, great and many, indicating the existence of the Creator, Most High, His oneness, the perfection of His power, and His far-reaching wisdom, of whose requirements is what they denied: the sending of the Messenger, the sending down of the Book, the clarifying of the paths of guidance, and the designation of the pits of ruin ﴿for a people who are mindful of God﴾, Most High, and who beware of the consequence. He, glory be to Him, specified them by mention because mindfulness (taqwa) is what calls to reflection and contemplation.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 10, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ is an explanation of the state of those who disbelieve in the Resurrection, which was alluded to earlier, and who turn away from the clear signs that point to it. By "their meeting with Him, exalted is His glory," what is meant is either returning to Him for the Resurrection or meeting the reckoning. Either way, together with the shift to the divine name (the Majestic Name), there is in it a magnification of the matter that is not hidden.

Al-raja' (expectation, hope) is applied to expecting good, as in al-amal (hope), and to fear and expecting harm, and to general expectation. In the first sense it is literal, and in the last two it is figurative. Some of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqin) chose the last, figurative meaning, which encompasses both hope and fear. So the meaning is: they do not expect the return to Us, or the meeting of Our reckoning that leads either to a good reward or to a bad punishment. Thus they do not hope for the first, nor do they fear the second. Pointing to their lack of hope is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and they are content with the worldly life﴾, for it indicates the preference of the lowly and base over the lofty and precious. And pointing to their lack of fear is His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿and they feel secure in it﴾, for what is meant is that they settled in it with the settling of one who will never move on, safe from the arrival of alarming things, not bringing to mind what would distress them of punishment.

It is also permissible that al-raja' be taken in the first sense, with the sentence elliptical (containing an omitted mudaf, a governed noun), meaning: they do not hope for the good meeting with Us through resurrection and revival into eternal life, and they are content instead of it, and of the noble honours in it, with the worldly life, which is perishing and base, and they settle into it, devoting themselves to it, confining the focus of their aspirations to its pleasures and adornments, with no diverting force turning them away and no inclining factor bending them back.

It is also permissible that it be taken in the second sense, with the sentence likewise elliptical: they do not fear the evil of Our meeting, which ought to be feared. This was objected to on the ground that the word "content with the worldly life" rejects this, for it indicates what came before, namely abandoning the higher and taking the lower.

The Imam said: taking al-raja' to mean fear is far-fetched, because interpreting a word by its opposite is not permissible. It is not hidden that this is open to dispute, for it has been attested in their usage, and al-Raghib mentioned it, and al-Imam al-Marzuqi, and they cited as evidence the verse of Abu Dhu'ayb:

When the bee stings him, he does not hope for its sting, and he has made a pact with it in a house of wool, [its] workers.

Al-Raghib justified this by saying that hope and fear imply each other. As for the objection to the Imam that using an opposite for its opposite is permissible in the sarcastic metaphor (al-istiʿarah al-tahakkumiyyah, the ironic metaphor), this is not valid, for the intent of his mercy-bestowed Lord, may Allah have mercy on him, is that this is not permissible outside the aforementioned metaphor, as his words "an interpretation, not a metaphor" indicate. Furthermore, it is not permissible to consider this metaphor applicable here, because irony is not intended, as is not hidden.

It is known from what we have mentioned in the explanation of the verse that the particle bi (in "bihā") is for location (the sense of "in"). It is also permissible that it be for cause (sababiyyah), meaning: they settled because of its adornments and ornaments. The choice of the past-tense form in the last two traits is to indicate their certainty and establishment, just as the choice of the future-tense form in the first indicates continuity.

﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾, which are detailed in the pages of the cosmos, as some of them were indicated, or Our revealed signs that alert to reasoning from them, which agree with them in indicating the truth of what they do not hope for of the meeting that follows resurrection, and in indicating the falsehood of what they were content with and felt secure in of the worldly life. ﴿are heedless﴾: they do not reflect upon them at all, even if they were warned by what they were warned by, because of their immersion in what keeps them from them, of the petty circumstances. The repetition of the relative pronoun is to lead to this clause, which indicates the continuance and persistence of their heedlessness. The conjunction (the 'atf, coordination) is because the described attribute differs from those before it among the attributes. In this there is an indication that they combine this and that, and that each of the two is distinct and independent, fit to be a source of blame and threat. The saying that this is due to the difference between the two attributes, and the alerting that the threat is for combining the total oblivion of the signs with immersion in lusts, such that the Hereafter never crosses their minds at all, is not valid, since it is understood from its apparent meaning that neither of them on its own necessitates the threat, rather the combination necessitates it, and this, as you see, is not so. And that it is for the difference between the two groups, by intending by the first those who denied the Resurrection and intended only the worldly life, and by the second those whom love of the immediate has diverted from reflecting on the deferred and preparing for it, like the People of the Book whom love of the world and leadership diverted from faith and preparation for the Hereafter, is extremely far-fetched in this context.

Page 73

"Those": that is, those described by what was mentioned.
